title: Five-Paragraph Essay
description: WRITING STRUCTURE: Five-Paragraph Essay. essay Sections: Introduction; Body paragraph 1; Body paragraph 2; Body paragraph 3; Conclusion. Worked example included in this record. The five-paragraph essay is training wheels for argument, not the shape of all good writing.
demo:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Writing-structure demo: verifies the breakdown and example."""
BREAKDOWN = [('Introduction', 'Hook the reader and state the thesis as the last sentence.'), ('Body paragraph 1', 'First supporting point with one piece of evidence.'), ('Body paragraph 2', 'Second supporting point with one piece of evidence.'), ('Body paragraph 3', 'Strongest point or counterargument rebuttal.'), ('Conclusion', 'Restate the thesis in new words and widen to the bigger picture.')]
EXAMPLE = 'Intro: School gardens teach more than gardening. Thesis: every school should have one. Body 1: students learn biology hands-on. Body 2: gardens build responsibility. Body 3: critics cite cost, but grants cover it. Conclusion: a garden is a classroom that grows.'
assert len(BREAKDOWN) >= 3, 'a structure needs at least 3 sections'
assert all(s and p for s, p in BREAKDOWN), 'every section needs a purpose'
assert len(EXAMPLE) > 40, 'example must be a real worked example'
print('OK: %d-section structure, worked example (%d chars)' % (len(BREAKDOWN), len(EXAMPLE)))
provenance: Public reference compilation. Each record below is an original working example composed for this archive; record types are standard real-world kinds.
